gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the $17,833.09 FreeScan UE Pro2 price ChatGPT showed is no US price at all: it equals 3D Printing Canada's CAD 24,999 listing converted to dollars. It also gives no US price for the EinScan Rigil ($4,999 at MatterHackers) or the FreeScan Combo+ ($14,999 at Top3DShop). 3D Scanner Match, the cited buyer page, marks all three 'quote needed'.
standout_why: I compared against 3dscannermatch.com/3d-scanners/reverse-engineering (cited twice), invenio3d.com.au (cited) and trimechmanufacturing.com SHINING 3D Buyers Guide 2026 (cited). 3D Scanner Match already lists the low end: MetroX $749, MetroX Pro $907, Raptor $879 and Raptor Pro $1,499. It also already gives Raptor plus QUICKSURFACE Lite as $1,419. For the HandySCAN BLACK Elite, FreeScan Combo and EinScan Rigil it shows 'quote needed', with no prices. Invenio gives only price tiers ('Premium', 'Entry to mid'). TriMech gives no prices at all. None of them prices the $5k to $25k band, and none notices that ChatGPT's UE Pro2 price is a converted Canadian listing.
decides: This confirms the budget pick and does not overturn it. The MetroX line, from $749 on Revopoint's store, stays the value choice. The next step up costs real money: the EinScan Rigil is $4,999 with no CAD software listed, and its laser volumetric accuracy of 0.04 + 0.06 mm/m is looser than the 0.02 + 0.04 mm/m MetroX Pro figure on our page. The first verifiable US price at metrology grade is the Combo+ at $14,999. The UE Pro2 has no US list price ChatGPT could show, and Creaform sells only by quote. So the page can tell a shopper under about $5k that every listed figure above the MetroX/Raptor tier is either a quote or a Canadian price.
